children: Assets under management (AUM) of gold and silver exchange-traded funds (ETFs) have expanded significantly over the past year, with gold ETF assets rising 1.8 times and silver ETF assets increasing 1.7 times, according to the October 2026 Mutual Fund Industry Dashboard by Franklin Templeton.
Gold ETF AUM stood at ₹1.80 lakh crore in October 2026, compared with ₹1.02 lakh crore in the same month last year. Silver ETF assets rose to ₹70,000 crore from ₹43,000 crore during the period.
Together, the two categories managed assets worth ₹2.5 lakh crore at the end of October, compared with ₹1.45 lakh crore a year earlier.

The growing asset base has also increased the share of commodities in the broader passive investment universe. Commodities accounted for 16% of the assets under management of ETFs and index funds in October 2026, compared with 11% a year ago, the dashboard showed.

The report's breakdown of ETF assets shows gold ETFs accounting for 16% and silver ETFs for 6% of total ETF assets in October 2026. Equity ETFs continued to account for the largest share at 70%, while debt ETFs made up 8%.

The expansion in precious metal ETFs comes against the backdrop of a broader increase in passive investment assets. The dashboard put the combined AUM of ETFs and index funds at ₹15.24 lakh crore in October 2026, compared with ₹13.67 lakh crore a year earlier, an increase of 11.5%.
Overall, the mutual fund industry's AUM stood at ₹83.39 lakh crore in October 2026, up 4.4% from ₹79.88 lakh crore a year earlier.

title: Gold, silver ETF AUM nearly double in a year; gold funds lead the rise: Franklin Templeton
